title: Corned Beef Hash
subtitle: A skillet fry of corned beef, potato, and onion
excerpt: Diced potato and onion fried in a cast-iron skillet until crisp, then folded through tinned corned beef and pressed into a golden cake. A diner standard that asks only for a good pan and patience.
sourceNotes: American diner staple, adapted from traditional American short-order cooking.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Boil the potatoes ahead and refrigerate. Cold cooked potato crisps better than raw in the pan.

content.text: Corned beef hash is a diner dish of crisp potato and onion with salty, soft corned beef pressed into a unified cake in a cast-iron pan. The crust comes from leaving it alone. Resist the urge to stir too often, and it will reward you with a proper golden base.
Put the diced potato in a saucepan of cold salted water. Bring to a boil and cook for 5 minutes until just tender but not soft. Drain well and leave to steam dry for a few minutes.
Heat the oil and butter in the cast-iron skillet over a medium-high heat until the butter foams.
Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes until softened. Add the green pepper if using and cook for 2 more minutes.
Add the parboiled potato. Spread into a single layer and press down firmly. Cook without stirring for 5 to 6 minutes until the base is browned and crisp.
Fold the corned beef through the potato mixture. Season with salt, pepper, and Worcestershire sauce if using. Press everything down firmly into the pan.
Cook for another 6 to 8 minutes, pressing down every couple of minutes and allowing a crust to form. Flip sections of the hash to expose the crust upward.
Serve straight from the pan with a fried or poached egg on top if you like.

items.symptom: The hash is grey and soft, with no crust.
items.cause: The pan was too cool or the mixture was stirred too often.
items.fix: Use a heavy cast-iron pan. Get it hot before the fat goes in. Press down firmly and leave it alone for a few minutes at a time.

items.symptom: The corned beef breaks down to mush.
items.cause: The beef was added too early and cooked too long.
items.fix: Fold it in once the potato has already crisped, and do not stir again after pressing.

items.cause: Not enough fat or the heat was too high.
items.fix: Use a combination of oil and butter, and reduce the heat slightly if the pan smokes heavily.
